title: War of Brilliants
reviewNotes: Four selected branches from seven-piece position after ...Qc6. Correct captioned Rxc4 to visually supported Rxe4+. Main source b8=N+ forks Qd7 after checking preparation. b8=Q allows ...Qc6+ Qb7+ Qxb7 actual mate. Separate saved ...Qb8+ diagram yields actual stalemate after either Kxb8 or Qxb8; intervening queen maneuvers not encoded as a continuous branch.
transcript: White seems to be completely lost. It does have a pawn that it can try to push to get a new queen, but black is simply going to pin this pawn and now there is no way to promote it. But fortunately, white has the brilliant shot bishop to D7 sacrificing the bishop to pin the queen to the king and of course the queen has to take or it's going to get captured. But after it does, white can now promote to a queen. Not. Because if you do promote to a queen, black actually always has a check and this is going to lead to a repetition. So white has to find the very precise rook takes C4 check first. And now after the king moves, you would think that we are free to promote to a queen, but again this doesn't work. Although we are defending a key checking square, black has a brilliant resource. It's going to push the king up and then play the majestic queen to B8 check and no matter how you recapture this queen, both of these moves are going to lead to a stalemate [music] and thus draw. So how does white possibly win here? Well, it can continue with another check with the rook to E5 check. Now if the king goes down, we can safely promote. The trick doesn't work anymore. And if the king ever steps to one of these squares, we can promote with a check. But what's interesting is what happens after king to A6. It seems like black is simply out of the woods. We cannot promote to a queen because after this check, we are actually going to get checkmated. But of course, white can just [music] promote to a knight with a check on the king. The king has to move. The queen is going [music] to fall and this is going to be a textbook win for white.
